summary: Created a 5-phase implementation plan from the research report for fixing the baier_katoen_2008 section07 chunk anomaly. Phase 1 captures the baseline (12 sibling chunk counts 128/111/106/99/110/101/1/112/107/111/113/79, 1,177 total rows, and reconfirms the stale giant-chunk chunk_id a6b60aa1fca40ca4). Phase 2 applies the fix -- removing the early `return [(chunk_content, True)]` at extension-source line 278 inside subdivide_chunk()'s oversized-atomic branch so oversized atomic-classified chunks fall through to the existing paragraph/sentence subdivision -- and keeps the extension-source and deployed copies byte-identical (diff -q, task #841 drift guard). Phase 3 re-chunks ONLY section07 (clears the stale single-chunk output, re-runs literature-chunk.sh against part07 into .chunks/section07, research-verified to produce ~94 chunks). Phase 4 explicitly DELETEs the stale chunk_id a6b60aa1fca40ca4 row from the live .literature.db (required because chunk_id is content-hashed, so re-chunking does NOT auto-replace it) and then reindexes via literature-build-index.sh --global. Phase 5 verifies section07 ~94 chunks, no regression on the other 11 sections or 93 covered dirs, drift guard (diff -q), check-extension-docs.sh exits 0, and the Job 4 94/3 covered/uncovered invariant. Waves: [[1,2],[3],[4],[5]]; estimated 2 hours.

decisions_made: Structured the fix as 5 small phases with an explicit baseline-capture phase up front so no-regression can be verified against recorded sibling chunk counts and the stale chunk_id can be reconfirmed before the DB delete
Made Phase 1 (baseline) and Phase 2 (code fix) an independent first wave since capturing baseline numbers does not depend on the code edit; re-chunk (Phase 3) depends on both

Kept the DB delete + reindex in a dedicated phase (Phase 4) after re-chunk, because the stale content-hashed chunk_id must be removed explicitly before --global reindex or it persists as an orphaned 46K-token duplicate

Scoped re-chunking to section07 only (clear its output dir, re-run the chunker against part07 alone) rather than a full-corpus re-chunk, and relied on --global reindex being content-idempotent for the 93 unaffected directories
Excluded the blackburn_2002 legacy issue and the optional docstring documentation note from scope, per the research report's out-of-scope classification
